Subject: Curevation DPA redlines + MSA tie-outs

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attached is our redline of Redwood’s DPA (Curevation_DPA_Redline_v1.docx) and a short SCCs impact summary. Main asks from our side:

- Confirm controller/processor roles for the analytics exports (section 2.1) — we want explicit processor commitments for subprocessor vetting.
- Add a short transfer impact addendum for UK/EU exports with fallback routing options.
- Retain current deletion SLA for customer data (30 days) but allow a narrow exception for backup retention (up to 90 days) with encryption-at-rest commitments.

We’re also tracking a handful of Order Form items in MSA_OrderForm_Tracker.xlsx — redlines touching pricing triggers if the dedicated routing is required. Can you confirm whether Redwood can sign the DPA with these items as-is or whether we need a short redline call with legal?

Attachment: Curevation_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (docx)
Attachment: SCCs_Impact_Summary.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Jacob Martin
Senior Counsel, Curevation Health

Subject: Re: Curevation DPA redlines + MSA tie-outs

Jacob —

Received, thanks for the clear summary and the tracker. Quick read-through from our side:

- Processor obligations: we can accept a stronger verification clause for subprocessor onboarding, but need to map which subprocessors Curevation expects to evaluate vs. those covered by our standard attestation.
- Transfer addendum: we typically propose EU SCCs + a fallthrough 'regional routing' commitment for customers that require UK-only residency. Need to confirm route availability with infra ops.
- Deletion SLA exception for backups: acceptable if we add a short operational note (encrypted backups, access controls, documented retention schedule).

Looping in Ben and Laura to coordinate legal redlines and procurement pricing impacts. Can Ben/Laura pull the MSA_OrderForm_Tracker into the procurement playbook and let Jacob know what pricing delta, if any, the dedicated routing would create?

I’m available for a 30-min redline call tomorrow afternoon (UTC) if that helps.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jacob Martin <jacob.martin@curevation.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Curevation DPA redlines + MSA tie-outs

Thanks — quick procurement read:

- Dedicated routing: estimate a ~12-18% surcharge on base inference usage if Curevation requires per-tenant regional pools (depends on length of commit). I’ll add a line item to the tracker (MSA_OrderForm_Tracker.xlsx).
- Deletion SLA: operational exception for backups is fine; pricing unaffected. We should ensure the exception is scoped (only for system-level backups, not exported customer CSVs).
- SCCs fallback: operationally possible but requires a short lead time for dedicated capacity (2–3 weeks for provisioning).

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal redline call to align on language (Sofia + Laura + Curevation counsel) — 30 minutes.
2) We publish a slightly edited DPA (Redwood_DPA_response_v1.docx) during the call and track final Order Form pricing in the tracker.

Laura — can you pick 15:30–17:30 UTC windows tomorrow? I’ll send a calendar invite and include our infra ops note for provisioning times.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal, Contracts & Procurement, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
